st.headline: Unitree soars in Shanghai debut, a milestone for China’s humanoid robotics sector
st.teaser: The stock was changing hands at 900 yuan on the tech-focused STAR Market in early trade, compared with its IPO price of 150.8 yuan.
fullText: SHANGHAI/BEIJING - Shares in Unitree, China’s best-known humanoid robot maker, soared nearly sixfold in its Shanghai trading debut, in a landmark moment for the country’s robotics sector, which has become a key battleground in the Sino-US tech war.

While Unitree, which competes with Hyundai Motor Group-owned Boston Dynamics and Tesla, is not the first Chinese humanoid robot maker to list, its listing is expected to set the tone for a slew of other rivals preparing to come to market.

The stock was changing hands at 900 yuan on the tech-focused STAR Market in early trade, compared with its IPO price of 150.8 yuan. It pared some gains after having opened at the day’s high of 1,100 yuan.

The world’s biggest humanoid-robot maker by sales, which raised roughly US$900 million (S$1.1 billion) in its initial public offering last week, has drawn global attention for its robots that run, dance and perform martial arts.
It is also, unlike most of its peers, profitable even if few of its robots are used in commercial applications.
Investors are also drawn to Unitree’s perceived state support as China seeks to gain the upper hand in tech over the United States and pushes development of the sector.

Its founder Wang Xingxing had a coveted front-row seat at a summit with tech business leaders hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping early last year, and the start-up also has backing from some of China’s most influential tech firms including Tencent, Alibaba and DeepSeek.
“It is a top-tier player, and its uniqueness commands premiums,” said Yan Kai, a venture capitalist and partner at Ivy Capital in Shanghai.
“Its price is dictated by political and economic considerations, rather than valuation models.”

The debut coincides with the opening of the World Robot Conference in Beijing, where hundreds of mostly Chinese companies will be launching new products and demonstrating advancements that the government is betting will make up for the labour shortfall caused by China’s demographic crisis.
Some 10 per cent of the Unitree shares were sold in the IPO, and Wang continues to own around a fifth of the company.
The debut has catapulted his personal wealth to more than US$12 billion on paper. Reuters

cna.headline: Iman Fandi performs at Snoop Dogg’s Los Angeles music event, debuts upcoming single
cna.teaser: The 26-year-old Singaporean singer performed at an invitation-only live music event in Los Angeles, California, where she debuted her upcoming single It Is.
fullText: Singaporean singer Iman Fandi performed at a live music event in Los Angeles, California, headlined by American rapper Snoop Dogg on Aug 15, where she made the international debut of her upcoming single, It Is.

The performance came days after the 26-year-old performed her NDP 2026 song Giants, written by Weish, at the National Day Parade on Aug 9. On Tuesday (Aug 18), Iman shared photos and videos from the event on Instagram, calling the experience “a milestone I’ll never forget”.

“Still can’t believe I got to share the stage with Snoop Dogg and so many incredible, talented and kind artists,” she wrote. “I’m beyond grateful to have been part of such a special evening here in Los Angeles.”
Iman also responded to a commenter who asked what it was like meeting Snoop Dogg, describing him as “super nice” and “super tall”.

View this post on Instagram The event, Superstar Among Friends: Broadus Together, was held at The Compound, Snoop Dogg’s private studio and office space in Los Angeles, and presented through TikTok Live Premiere and Death Row Records.

Other performers included Snoop Dogg’s son Corde Broadus, also known as Kalvin Love, and daughter Cori Broadus, as well as Filipino-Australian singer-songwriter Ylona Garcia, American R&B singer-songwriter Jane Handcock, soul singer Charlie Bereal and actor-singer O’Neal McKnight.
According to posts by performers including Iman, the invitation-only event drew more than 1 million viewers through its livestream.
Iman's upcoming single, It Is, is scheduled for release on Aug 21.

economistArticle.title: The Mirage of the Market: Why Stock Indices Mask Economic Reality
paras: For decades, stock market indices like the S&P 500 or Singapore's Straits Times Index have been treated as barometers of national economic health. When the charts trend upward, politicians boast of prosperity, and investors celebrate growing wealth. Yet, this correlation is increasingly becoming a historic relic, as the mechanisms governing stock indices diverge dramatically from the underlying reality of corporate performance and daily economic life.

The primary culprit behind this disconnect is the top-heavy nature of modern indices. In major market indices, capitalization-weighted methodologies mean that a handful of tech behemoths dominate the entire movement of the average. If three or four trillion-dollar companies experience a surge, the index climbs, painting a picture of robust growth even if the remaining hundreds of constituent companies are floundering under high debt and stagnant sales.

Furthermore, the modern equity market is heavily distorted by passive investing. As millions of retail investors put their savings into index funds, capital is automatically funneled into the largest companies regardless of their actual business fundamentals. This self-reinforcing loop artificially inflates the valuation of index giants while starving smaller, potentially innovative enterprises of much-needed capital, creating an illusion of widespread financial vitality.

Beyond valuation quirks, the divergence is driven by the rise of private markets. Many of the fastest-growing and most resilient firms choose to remain private far longer, funded by venture capital and private equity. Consequently, public stock exchanges are increasingly populated by mature, slow-growing legacy companies, meaning the public index represents a shrinking, less dynamic slice of the actual economic landscape.

For individual investors and policymakers alike, relying on these distorted aggregates is dangerous. A booming index can easily blind regulators to systemic vulnerabilities, such as rising corporate insolvencies or declining consumer purchasing power. To navigate this landscape, one must look beyond the deceptive simplicity of market indices and dissect the microeconomic realities that lie beneath the surface.
economistArticle.cn: 几十年来，诸如标准普尔500指数或新加坡海峡时报指数等股市指数一直被视为国家经济健康的晴雨表。当图表呈上升趋势时，政客们吹嘘繁荣，投资者庆祝财富增长。然而，这种相关性正日益成为历史遗迹，因为支配股票指数的机制与公司业绩和日常经济生活的底层现实发生了急剧分歧。这种脱节的首要罪魁祸首是现代指数“头重脚轻”的特质。在主要的市场指数中，市值权重法意味着少数科技巨头主导了整个指数的走势。如果三四家万亿美元级的公司出现飙升，指数就会攀升，描绘出一幅强劲增长的画面，即使其余数百家成份股公司正因高负债和销售停滞而苦苦挣扎。此外，现代股市受到被动投资的严重扭曲。随着数百万散户投资者将储蓄投入指数基金，资金会自动流入最大的公司，而不管它们的实际业务基本面如何。这种自我强化的循环人为地推高了指数巨头的估值，同时使规模较小、具有潜在创新能力的企业缺乏急需的资金，创造了一种广泛财务活力的幻觉。除了估值上的奇特现象，这种分歧还受到私募市场崛起的推动。许多增长最快、最具韧性的公司在风险投资和私募股权的资助下，选择保持私有化的时间要长得多。因此，公开证券交易所中成熟、增长缓慢的传统企业越来越多，这意味着公开指数代表的只是实际经济版图中不断缩小、活力较低的一部分。对于个人投资者和政策制定者而言，依赖这些失真的综合数据是危险的。蓬勃发展的指数极易使监管机构对系统性脆弱性视而不见，例如不断上升的企业破产率或不断下降的消费者购买力。要应对这一局势，人们必须看透市场指数那具有欺骗性的简单外表，剖析隐藏在表面之下的微观经济现实。

gems.s: If three or four trillion-dollar companies experience a surge, the index climbs, painting a picture of robust growth even if the remaining hundreds of constituent companies are floundering under high debt and stagnant sales.
gems.why: This sentence employs a vivid participle phrase ('painting a picture...') to show immediate consequence, contrasted against a concessive clause ('even if...') to expose a stark economic irony. / 这句话运用了生动的分词短语（'painting a picture...'）来展示直接后果，并与一个让步从句（'even if...'）进行对比，以揭示赤裸裸的经济讽刺。
